issues.legal_issue: A lease made contrary to statutory controls on letting remains binding between the landlord and tenant when the control scheme does not make the lease void and leaves enforcement to the regulator’s discretion.
material_facts: Landlords sought to treat leases as void because the required vacancy notifications had not been given and the prescribed letting process had not been followed.
The control scheme empowered the regulator to take steps to enforce compliance but did not require the regulator to evict every person who entered into possession contrary to the controls.
The disputes were proceedings between the landlords and their tenants.
issues.conclusion: The leases were not void, and neither party could assail them in a proceeding between the parties on the ground that they contravened the letting controls.
issues.legal_principle: Under clauses 22, 23 and 28 of the Central Provinces and Berar Letting of Houses and Rent Control Order, 1949, a lease made contrary to the letting controls is not void where the scheme provides discretionary enforcement and does not declare the lease void. The lease remains binding between its parties and cannot be avoided by either in a dispute between them. This follows Murlidhar Agarwal v. State of U.P., which approved Udhoo Dass v. Prem Prakash; Waman Shrinivas Kini v. Ratilal Bhagwandas & Co. was distinguished because it concerned enforcement of a statutory right to evict arising directly from a breach.

predicates.dispute_between_lease_parties: The landlord and tenant disputed the effect of their lease in a proceeding between them.
predicates.lease_made_in_breach_of_letting_controls: The landlord and tenant entered into a lease without following the applicable statutory requirements for letting the premises.
predicates.regulator_has_discretionary_enforcement_: The governing control scheme allowed the regulator to take enforcement steps but did not require it to do so in every case.

issues.definition: When parties dispute a lease made contrary to letting controls and the regulator has discretion over enforcement, the lease cannot be avoided by either party in their proceedings against one another.

issues.legal_issue: An exemption notification that describes a category of properties by reference to when they were constructed operates prospectively unless its terms indicate retroactive effect.
material_facts: A notification exempted non-residential properties constructed before a stated cutoff from specified letting controls.
The tenancy at issue began before the notification was issued.
The notification contained no indication that the exemption was to operate retroactively.
issues.conclusion: The notification operated prospectively only, so it did not exempt the tenancy that began before the notification was issued.
issues.legal_principle: Clause 30 of the Central Provinces and Berar Letting of Houses and Rent Control Order, 1949 authorized exemptions by notification. The date used to describe the category of properties covered by an exemption does not, without more, establish the period during which the exemption operates; the notification here was prospective.

predicates.proceeding_concerning_exemption_notifica: The parties disputed whether a notification exempting a category of properties applied to their tenancy.
predicates.notification_describes_preexisting_prope: The notification identified covered properties by describing them as having been constructed before a specified cutoff.
predicates.notification_has_no_retroactive_indicati: The notification contained no language indicating that the exemption applied retroactively.

issues.definition: If a dispute concerns an exemption notification describing a preexisting property category and the notification gives no indication of retroactive effect, the exemption operates only prospectively.

issues.legal_issue: A concurrent finding of fact is not interfered with in a special-leave appeal when the Supreme Court is asked to revisit that finding.
material_facts: In a special-leave appeal, the appellant disputed the lower courts’ concurrent finding that a vacancy had occurred and a tenancy had been created.
The trial court and the High Court had reached the same factual finding.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court did not interfere with the concurrent factual finding.
issues.legal_principle: The Supreme Court declined to disturb the concurrent finding of fact in the exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution.

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The matter came before the Supreme Court as an appeal by special leave.
predicates.lower_courts_made_concurrent_factual_fin: The trial court and the High Court reached the same finding on a disputed fact.

issues.definition: In a special-leave appeal where the lower courts made the same factual finding, that finding is not reopened.
